sentences.text: I'm Emily, your host.
This podcast is for people who are learning English.
If you are an A1 level learner, don't worry.
I will speak slowly and clearly
so you can understand everything.
In today's episode, we are going to talk about Australia,
a beautiful country in the Southern Hemisphere.
Let's get started.
Part one, introduction to Australia.
Australia is a large country.
It is an island and a continent.
Australia is in the southern part of the world
and it is surrounded by the sea.
The capital city of Australia is Canberra,
but the biggest and most famous city is Sydney.
Sydney is known for its beautiful beach
and the famous opera house.
People from many different countries live in Australia.
Part two, geography of Australia.
Australia has many different types of land.
In the east, there are big mountains
called the Great Dividing Range.
These mountains are not very high,
but they are long and cover a lot of land.
In the center of Australia,
there is a very dry and hot place called the Outback.
The Outback has deserts and is very different
from the cities near the coast.
The weather can be very hot in the Outback.
In the west, Australia has some very beautiful beaches
and rainforests.
The country is also famous for its Great Barrier Reef,
which is the world's largest coral reef.
Many people visit Australia to see the reef and go diving.
Part three, animals in Australia.
Australia is famous for its unique animals.
One of the most famous animals is the kangaroo.
Kangaroos live in the wild and can hop very high.
You can also see koalas,
which are small animals that sleep in trees.
They look very cute.
Another famous animal is the platypus.
The platypus is a strange animal
because it lays eggs and has a beak like a duck.
Australia also has many dangerous animals,
like snakes and spiders.
But don't worry,
these animals usually stay in the wild
and people are careful to avoid them.
Part four, the food of Australia.
In Australia, people eat a lot of different foods.
Barbecue is very popular in Australia.
People cook meat on a grill and eat it with salads and bread.
It is called an Aussie Baba Queue.
You will find many people having a barbecue
in their gardens or parks.
Another famous food is Vegemite.
Vegemite is a dark, salty spread
that people put on bread or crackers.
Some people love it and some people don't like it at all.
If you visit Australia, you can try it
and see if you like it.
People in Australia also eat meat pies.
These are small pies filled with meat, gravy and vegetables.
They are very tasty and easy to eat for lunch or dinner.
Part five, sports in Australia.
Australians love sports.
The most popular sport in Australia
is Australian rules football.
This sport is a bit like soccer and rugby,
but it has different rules.
Many people watch the games
and cheer for their favorite teams.
Another popular sport in Australia is cricket.
Cricket is a game played with a bat and ball,
and people play it in parks and on the beach.
Swimming is also very popular
because Australia has many beautiful beaches.
Australia is also famous for its great athletes,
like Kathy Freeman,
who won a gold medal in the Olympics.
Part six, famous places to visit in Australia.
Australia has many famous places to visit.
One of the most famous places is the Sydney Opera House.
This building looks like a giant sailboat
and is on the water.
People go to the Opera House to watch concerts,
plays and dance performances.
Another famous place is Uluru, also called Ayers Rock.
Uluru is a very big rock
in the middle of Australia,
and it is very special to the Aboriginal people.
Many visitors come to see it
and learn about its cultural importance.
Australia also has many beautiful beaches.
Some of the most famous beaches
are Bondi Beach and Sydney
and White Haven Beach in Queensland.
These beaches have white sand and clear water,
and many people go there to swim, surf and relax.
Closing, that's all for today's episode.
I hope you learned something new about Australia.
It is a country with beautiful nature,
amazing animals and fun activities.
If you ever have the chance to visit,
make sure to try an Aussie Baba queue,
see the Opera House and visit Uluru.
of Slow English Podcast.
I hope you enjoyed it and learned some new words in English.
Bye.
